title: Shortbread
subtitle: crisp, buttery Scottish biscuits with a crumbling texture
excerpt: Shortbread has three ingredients and two rules: use good butter and do not overwork the dough. The result is a biscuit so rich and crumbly that it barely holds together. It is one of the great things in British baking.
sourceNotes: Scottish in origin. The basic shortbread recipe has been unchanged for centuries.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze baked biscuits. Defrost at room temperature for 30 minutes.
recipe.batchNotes: Double easily. The dough keeps in the fridge for 3 days.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make the dough, wrap, and refrigerate. Slice and bake within 3 days.
recipe.temperatureNote: Conventional oven -- low heat for pale, sandy shortbread

content.text: The dough should come together without needing much kneading. If it is too crumbly to hold, press it together in your hands. Do not add liquid. The more you work shortbread dough, the less short it becomes. Stop as soon as it coheres.
Beat the softened butter and caster sugar together until just combined -- not fluffy, just mixed. Add the flour and salt. Bring together into a dough with your hands. Do not over-mix.
Press the dough into a log about 5cm in diameter. Wrap in cling film and refrigerate for 30 minutes. Alternatively, press into a lined tin for slab shortbread.
Heat the oven to 160C. Slice the log into rounds about 8mm thick. Place on lined baking sheets with a little space between each.
Bake for 18 to 20 minutes until pale golden at the edges. They should not colour much -- pale is the goal for the authentic sandy texture. Dust with caster sugar while still warm.
Leave on the tray to cool completely -- they are very fragile when warm and will firm up as they cool.

items.symptom: Shortbread is hard and tough rather than crumbly
items.fix: Mix only until the dough comes together. Stop immediately. The less you handle it, the shorter (more crumbly) the result.

items.symptom: Biscuits spread and lose their shape
items.cause: Butter was too warm, or dough not chilled before baking.
items.fix: Chill the sliced biscuits on the tray for 15 minutes before baking. Cold dough holds its shape better.

content.text: Shortbread is Scottish and has been made there since at least the 12th century. It was originally a refined form of medieval biscuit bread. In Scotland it is associated with Christmas and Hogmanay, given as gifts in decorative tins and eaten throughout the winter. It is now made and sold across Britain and recognised worldwide as one of Scotland's great food exports.
